formulations.Polymer system Notes: High-Mw poly(trimethylene carbonate) (PTMC) synthesized by bulk ring-opening polymerization of trimethylene carbonate with Sn(Oct)2 catalyst (Mη by GPC in CHCl3 = 368,000 g/mol, PDI = 1.36). Combined with LiTFSI at carbonate:Li molar ratios of n = 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21 (PTMCnLiTFSI) and solution-cast from acetonitrile into self-standing films.
formulations.Notes: n=2, richest-salt composition tested. Reported as tougher/leathery in texture vs. lower-salt samples, consistent with elevated Tg (Fig. 3b, plot only, no printed value). TGA onset of decomposition for the salt-richest sample ~190°C (Fig. 3a plot); pure PTMC (no salt) decomposes at ~260°C. Mη (368 kDa, viscosity-average, not Mn/Mw) and PDI 1.36 reported for the base polymer only, not per-formulation.
formulations.Reference: Sun, B.; Mindemark, J.; Edström, K.; Brandell, D. Polycarbonate-based solid polymer electrolytes for Li-ion batteries. Solid State Ionics 2013.

formulations.Notes: n=3. Reported as tougher/leathery in texture (along with n=2), consistent with elevated Tg vs. neat PTMC. formulations.Notes: n=5 (PTMC5LiTFSI). Used in LiFePO4/PTMC5LiTFSI/Li half-cell (Fig. 5): cycled at C/13 for 30 cycles at 60°C, then stored 28 days at 60°C, then cycled at C/55; discharge capacity plateaus at ~153 mAh/g with no fading over >120 days total (values read from digitized Fig. 5 plot, approximate). No conductivity value specifically reported for this ratio.

formulations.VFT Notes (above temp): Fig. 2a shows VTF-type conductivity vs. temperature with dashed VTF fit lines, but no numerical VFT prefactor/Ea/T0 are printed in the text; left null.
formulations.Notes: n=8 (PTMC8LiTFSI), one of the two best-performing electrolytes (with n=13). Text states conductivity 'in the order of' 1e-7 S/cm at 60°C and 1e-9 S/cm at 25°C for the two best ratios (n=8 and n=13) together — treated as an order-of-magnitude estimate, not individually resolved. Electrochemically stable to 5 V vs Li/Li+ (CV, 60°C, Fig. 4, dashed line, scanned down to 3 V). Also solution-cast onto LiFePO4 composite electrodes and 3D Cu-nanopillar substrates (SEM, Fig. 7) and used in fresh-vs-pre-stored LiFePO4 half-cell comparison (Fig. 6).
formulations.Reference: Sun, B.; Mindemark, J.; Edström, K.; Brandell, D. Polycarbonate-based solid polymer electrolytes for Li-ion batteries. Solid State Ionics 2013.
